key_facts: For about a week and a half, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly backed a harder line on Nvidia over national security risks tied to co-founder Jensen Huang's personal relationship with Alice Huang, whom the New York Times and others reported was a Chinese intelligence asset; by the weekend of the report Bessent had softened his opposition, and Nvidia's board reappointed Jensen Huang as CEO at President Trump's urging. In a Nov. 13 CNBC interview Bessent said 'any leakage is very frustrating... in the AI race it gives the Chinese an advantage,' and said Treasury and others wanted to blacklist Megaspeed, but 'Commerce has the pen.' Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick heads that department; Commerce has since tightened some restrictions on US chips to China.

Trump said he intervened because Nvidia's troubles caused a market plunge, which he attributed partly to Democrats' midterm victory: 'I watched our country lose $5 trillion because of a bad election.' Lutnick said in January that Trump was weighing whether to allow Nvidia to sell H200 chips to China, and Trump decided to go ahead with that deal.

Sen. Tom Cotton said 'I think we need to catalog the damage that's been done,' and said Lutnick had not responded to his letters. Trump said he was swayed by Xi meeting him at the plane during his China visit the prior week.
